item.title: FG steps up CNG push with fuel station revival, staff vehicle conversion
item.description: —Initiative promotes cheaper energy, attracts private investment — Perm Sec – –Says 10 JAC vehicles, Villa shuttle buses already CNG-hybrid By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA–The Federal Government has renewed its drive to promote the adoption of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) with the reopening of a former petrol filling station at the State House, Abuja, now converted into a CNG refuelling facility. Plans are also underway to extend vehicle conversion services to interested government personnel. The Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Fashedemi, stated that the initiative underscored the administration’s resolve to lead by example in promoting cost-effective and cleaner energy alternatives, while encouraging private-sector participation in the development of the country’s gas infrastructure. Speaking at the inauguration of the facility in Karu, Abuja, Fashedemi disclosed that the project was executed through a partnership between the State House, the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), and Rollin Energy Limited, with no expenditure incurred by the State House for its rehabilitation. He explained that the Federal Government deliberately made the abandoned facility available for conversion to demonstrate the viability of the presidential initiative and encourage private investors to take advantage of emerging opportunities in the CNG market. He further explained the initiative is also aimed at addressing concerns over the limited availability of CNG refuelling stations, which has continued to constrain wider adoption of the alternative fuel. Fashedemi said government’s responsibility was to create an enabling environment for private-sector participation rather than take over the business of establishing and operating commercial refuelling facilities. He urged business operators and prospective investors to partner with Pi-CNG to establish more stations and vehicle conversion centres across the country. “All the filling stations you see around, are they owned by government? No. They are owned by people and business operators. The earlier existing and prospective business people recognise this as an opportunity and partner with Pi-CNG to establish these facilities, the better,” he said. The Permanent Secretary disclosed that the State House had already commenced the integration of CNG technology into its vehicle fleet, with about 10 recently acquired JAC vehicles being hybrid models, alongside some shuttle buses operating within the Presidential Villa. He said the government was taking further steps to encourage interested State House personnel to convert eligible personal vehicles to CNG-hybrid systems in the coming weeks. “We are demonstrating that we are walking the talk of Mr President. In the next few weeks, a number of our staff will be bringing their vehicles here for conversion, subject to the eligibility of the vehicles,” he said. item.title: ‘We are on the ballot’ — Atiku vows to contest 2027 despite court ruling
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has rejected the latest court ruling affecting the African Democratic Congress (ADC), insisting that he will remain in the race for the 2027 presidential election. Atiku, in a statement issued on Friday, said the judgment nullifying the David Mark-led leadership of the party and his presidential nomination should not be mistaken for the will of Nigerians. “Let no one mistake the latest court ruling for the will of the Nigerian people. No manipulation, conjecture or concoction can erase our place in this contest, silence our campaign or deny Nigerians the right to choose their future,” he said. “We are on the ballot, and the people must be allowed to decide.” The former vice-president accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of deploying political pressure, court manoeuvres and other tactics to weaken opposition parties ahead of the election. He alleged that those in power were attempting to compromise the voters’ register through “AI-generated photographs, false names and fictitious identities”. Atiku said such actions were aimed at making genuine political competition difficult and pushing Nigeria towards a one-party state. He also challenged the ruling party to defend its record before voters rather than rely on its political strength. “Those who boast of having thirty-two governors and claim to have bought, pressured or coerced leaders from other parties into their fold should have no reason to fear a free and fair contest,” he said. Atiku criticised the Tinubu administration over the removal of fuel subsidy, the depreciation of the naira, rising food prices and worsening insecurity, arguing that the government had failed to ease the hardship facing Nigerians. He said businesses had shut down, young people were leaving the country in search of opportunities, while banditry and kidnapping continued to threaten communities. “Look around you. Market stalls stand empty. Feeding your family has become a daily struggle. Fuel prices keep rising, and silent pain fills homes across the country,” he said. Atiku urged his supporters not to lose hope, insisting that he would not withdraw from the presidential contest despite the legal challenge. “Let me be clear to every Nigerian who has stood with us: I am in this race. I am not going anywhere. We will be on the ballot,” he said. “No threat, blackmail or court manoeuvre will make me abandon you or the cause we share.” He vowed that the opposition would resist attempts to turn Nigeria into a one-party state and called on the ruling party to face its opponents in a free, fair and credible election. “If those in power believe in their numbers and their record, let us meet at the polls in a free, fair and credible contest,” Atiku said. item.title: Alaafin, number one ruler in Yorubaland – Oba Owoade
item.description: The Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Akeem Owoade I, has declared that he is the number one traditional ruler in Yorubaland, citing the historical significance and contributions of the old Oyo Empire to Yoruba civilisation. The monarch made the assertion during an interview on Edmund Obilo’s channel, where he spoke on Yoruba unity, the historical position of the Alaafin and his plans for the development of Oyo. Asked whether the Alaafin was the supreme king in Yorubaland, Oba Owoade answered in the affirmative, maintaining that history supported the position. “Historically, yes. If you want to go by history and the contribution of Oyo to Yoruba civilisation, then I would say that the Alaafin is number one,” he said. He, however, dismissed suggestions that he was in competition with other prominent Yoruba monarchs, particularly the Ooni of Ife, over traditional supremacy. “I don’t fight for supremacy or whatever with anybody,” he said. On his commitment to the Yoruba race, the monarch said he regularly prayed for the progress of the people, stressing that the success of Oyo would bring honour to the entire Yoruba race. “I believe that when Oyo succeeds, the Yoruba in their entirety get honoured. That’s my belief,” he said. Speaking on the development of Oyo, Oba Owoade expressed optimism about ongoing infrastructure projects, particularly the proposed circular road and its planned dualisation. He said the project, which would connect areas including Infinity and Sabo, would improve the city’s appearance and contribute to its development. The Alaafin also discussed the forthcoming Oyo Empire Day, describing it as a three-day celebration expected to attract about 40,000 people. He explained that the event was designed to bring together communities and people historically connected to the old Oyo Empire, irrespective of their present locations. According to him, the celebration would provide an opportunity to reconnect with their roots, preserve Yoruba culture and deliberate on the future of coming generations. Explaining why the event was named Oyo Empire Day rather than Oyo Day, the monarch said the empire had a wider historical reach beyond the present-day Oyo community. “The Oyo Empire comprises a number of people and cities, not just one. That’s why we are trying to make sure that we come together, reconnect to our roots, preserve our culture, deliberate on how to move forward and make a better future for our children together,” he said. Oba Owoade further disclosed that a Hall of Fame would be established as part of the celebration to recognise individuals and communities that had made significant contributions to Yoruba civilisation, Oyo Empire history, culture and heritage. He added that attendance would not be restricted to people with ancestral links to Oyo, noting that anyone interested in Yoruba culture was welcome. “Everybody is invited. item.title: How High Tariffs, Cost Of Living Made Trump Unpopular In US Midterm Elections — Rep-Elect Adesanya
item.description: Member-elect of the Georgia House of Representatives (District 43) in the United States, Solomon Adesanya, has explained how the struggles facing American residents, including high tariffs and the cost of living, played a major role in the outcome of the 2026 midterm elections. “I will tell you that this election was about something much bigger than political parties. It was about the everyday struggle of ordinary people. It was about the mother working two jobs who still struggles to put food on the table,” Adesanya said while on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Friday. “It was about the father who works 40 hours a week but still cannot afford to get decent housing. And it was ultimately about the millions of Americans who are doing everything right, working hard, playing by the rules, and yet find themselves falling further behind.” ﻿ According to him, the message from voters was clear: that hard work should lead to economic security, not a lifetime of financial struggle. “People are tired of an economy where the cost of living keeps rising. American people and the people of the great state of Georgia want to know that their government sees them, hears them, and is prepared to act on their behalf. And that’s the message that I take from this election, and that’s the responsibility that I intend to carry into the next legislative session,” the lawmaker said. Adesanya also noted that affordability had been a crisis since President Donald Trump got into the Oval Office. “We first started with this tariff war, and what you would find is when the president increased the tariffs on Canada and Mexico — one of our strongest allies by way of NAFTA — we’re hurting Americans, and Georgians were suffering that the cost of living had shot up in an unbelievable fashion and, added to the war in Iran, that was a war that nobody wanted and that war ultimately made the president unpopular,” the legislator stated. “When I get out and, you know, speaking with people in my community and my constituents, it is remarkable how people thought that they supported President Trump to be president and somehow think their life is going to be better and they’re going to become richer. The opposite happened. Their lives are worse off. “Our agenda is for the everyday Americans, not the Elon Musks, not the wealthy.” Adesanya said Nigerian politicians must know that elections are not about them but the communities they serve. He also disclosed his plan to champion the legislation that raises the Georgia minimum wage to $15 per hour. “So affordability is really crushing people. I mean, it’s unfortunate that we’re here, but people now see, and one of the things that I am looking forward to doing is when we get back in session, the next legislative session, I am ready to introduce legislation that increases the minimum wage to $15 per hour,” said Adesanya. “Over the past, what, 20 years? item.title: 2027: Heaven won’t fall if Atiku isn’t on the ballot — Keyamo
item.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has said Nigeria would not suffer any catastrophe if former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar is excluded from the ballot for the 2027 presidential election. Keyamo made the remark in a post on X on Friday while reacting to the Federal High Court judgment that nullified Atiku’s nomination as the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). The judgment, which also invalidated the David Mark-led executive of the party, has triggered reactions from political figures and opposition supporters. Keyamo questioned what he described as the inconsistent attitude of opposition parties towards the judiciary, arguing that political actors should respect court decisions regardless of whether they favour or hurt their interests. He recalled the Supreme Court’s 2019 judgment that invalidated the victories of All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in Zamfara State, from the governorship to the state House of Assembly, and declared their Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) opponents winners. Atiku, who contested the 2019 presidential election on the PDP platform, had welcomed the ruling at the time, describing it as a victory for the rule of law. In a statement issued by his media adviser, Paul Ibe, the former vice-president said: “Nothing is as pleasing to the ears of believers, as justice being served in the holy month of Ramadan.” Keyamo also cited the Supreme Court’s February 13, 2020, judgment that nullified the election of David Lyon, the APC candidate for Bayelsa governor, a day before his scheduled inauguration. The ruling paved the way for PDP candidate Douye Diri to emerge as governor. The minister said the APC accepted the court’s decisions without attacking the judiciary, adding that opposition parties should not condemn judges when rulings go against them. On February 13, 2020, when the Supreme Court nullified the victory of the APC Governorship candidate in Bayelsa State, David Lyon, a day to his swearing in (when he was in fact inspecting the stadium to be used), the APC took it with equanimity on the chin. item.title: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono considers quitting football after striker’s death – report
item.description: Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono is reportedly considering retiring from football after his collision with Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel, who died following the incident. Owono was playing for Andorra FC when he collided with De Miguel while attempting to clear the ball during a match on Monday, November 2, 2026. The Tenerife forward was left on the pitch following the challenge and was taken to hospital, where he died the following morning from what was described as “accidental chest trauma”. Owono was sent off for the challenge and has reportedly been struggling emotionally following the striker’s death. According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, the goalkeeper is considering walking away from professional football following the tragedy. Ana Maye, a close friend of Owono and general coordinator of the Equatorial Guinea men’s national team, said the incident had deeply affected him despite efforts to offer support. “No matter how much we tell him, he’s deeply saddened. “He’s very affected, especially for Jesús Miguel’s one-and-a-half-year-old son and for his widow. He doesn’t know how to handle all of this.” Jesus Owono, who has been receiving psychological support from his team, also released a statement expressing his grief following De Miguel’s death. In a social media post, he wrote: “These are the most difficult days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to process what has happened. “I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. “But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus.” De Miguel’s funeral was held in his hometown of Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo, on Thursday, November 5. Hundreds of mourners, including family members and prominent figures in Spanish football, attended the burial to pay their final respects. Among those present were Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and Spain national team coach Luis de la Fuente. Meanwhile, Maye disclosed that Owono’s family had also been subjected to abuse following the incident, with some people reportedly targeting his relatives online and in person. She said: “They’re calling Jesús’s brother a murderer. He’s being heckled by his teammates, and even some parents are insulting him.” Vanguard News The post Goalkeeper Jesus Owono considers quitting football after striker’s death – report appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Supreme Court justices placed on US visa ban, retiring jurist reveals
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — A retiring Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Uwani Abba-Aji, disclosed on Friday that some justices of the court had been placed on a visa ban by the United States of America. Justice Abba-Aji, speaking during a valedictory session held to mark her retirement from the bench, said the travel ban followed a judgment of the apex court that she described as widely misinterpreted. She said: “My time on the Supreme Court bench was filled with challenges, some of which have served as additional opportunities to stand firm on the side of justice, regardless of the consequences. “One of such challenging judgments was widely misinterpreted and led to a travel ban to the United States of America being imposed on all members of the panel, a ban which still holds today.” Even though Justice Abba-Aji did not mention the specific case that led to the imposition of a US visa ban on Supreme Court Justices, Vanguard understands that it was connected to the legal tussle that followed the 2019 governorship election in Imo State. A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court, which included the current Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and Justice Abba-Aji, had on January 14, 2020, nullified the election of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Emeka Ihedioha, and ordered the swearing-in of the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Hope Uzodimma, who had initially finished fourth in the governorship election. In the lead judgment delivered by the CJN, the apex court ordered the immediate withdrawal of the Certificate of Return that had already been issued to Ihedioha by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). It ordered that a fresh Certificate of Return be issued to Uzodimma as the validly elected governor of Imo State. To arrive at the decision, the apex court panel vacated the concurrent verdicts of both the Court of Appeal and the Imo State Governorship Election Petitions Tribunal, which had earlier affirmed the PDP candidate as winner of the gubernatorial contest. The panel went ahead to add election results from 388 polling units, amounting to 213,295 votes, which were tendered before the tribunal by a police officer who testified as PW-54, but which INEC disowned. After all the votes were computed inside the courtroom, Uzodimma was declared the candidate who secured the majority of lawful votes cast at the election, a judgment that elicited wide reactions and protests. Other members of the panel, which was led by the then CJN, Justice Tanko Muhammad, were Justices Sylvester Ngwuta, Kayode Ariwola and Amiru Sanusi. Although Ihedioha subsequently approached the apex court again for a review of the judgment, which he insisted occasioned a miscarriage of justice, his application was refused. item.title: Tinubu arrives in Akwa Ibom to inaugurate projects, attend APC rally
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital, for a working visit to inaugurate projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration and participate in an All Progressives Congress rally. Tinubu arrived in the state on Friday as part of a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers, marking his first major outing in the South-South since the APC began mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The President was welcomed at Victor Attah International Airport by Eno, government officials, APC leaders and a large crowd of supporters. During the visit, Tinubu is expected to inaugurate several projects at the airport, including its new international terminal building, the International Airport Hospital and the Ibom Aviation Village. He will also inaugurate the Airport-Okopedi Road, linking communities in Nsit Atai and Okobo Local Government Areas, and Ring Road 3, which connects Idoro Road to Ikot Ekpene Road through Uyo and Ibiono Ibom. Other projects scheduled for inauguration include the AKWA-GIS Office Complex, the Command and Control Centre and the ARISE Palm Resort. Following the project inaugurations, Tinubu is expected to attend an APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. item.title: Tinubu’s visit: Bus conveying women to welcome president involved in accident
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi Several people have sustained injuries on Wednesday after an Akwa Ibom State Transport Corporation (AKTC) bus conveying women to welcome President Bola Tinubu collided with a security vehicle along Oron Road, Uyo. The victims were reportedly among supporters mobilised to join Governor Umo Eno in welcoming the President, who arrived in Akwa Ibom State through Calabar for an official visit. The accident involved the bus, loaded with women heading towards the airport, and a security Hilux van with both vehicles were badly damaged in the collision, leaving several occupants injured and requiring emergency assistance. Nsikakabasi Akpan, who captured the aftermath of the accident, shared footage showing early responders and other persons struggling to evacuate injured victims from the wreckage of the vehicles. He described the incident as an accident along Oron Road involving a bus conveying women to the airport to receive the President and a security Hilux vehicle. Confirming the incident, Paul James, Public Relations Officer, Road Safety Operations, Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Akwa Ibom State Command, said the command had dispatched a response team to the scene. James, however, said the command was yet to establish the extent of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the collision. The reported accident cast a shadow over the build-up to Tinubu’s visit, which attracted supporters and political stakeholders who had gathered to receive the President and his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. The presidential couple were subsequently received by Governor Eno at the Victor Attah International Airport, Uyo, marking the commencement of their engagements in the state. The President’s official visit featured the unveiling of the airport’s new terminal, a major aviation infrastructure project expected to facilitate the commencement of international flight operations from the Victor Attah International Airport. The circumstances surrounding the crash, including the feared death and number of injured victims, were yet to be officially established by the FRSC as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Nine parties back ADC after David Mark’s leadership sack
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Nine opposition parties under the Coalition for Democracy have rallied behind the African Democratic Congress ADC, describing Thursday’s Federal High Court judgment which dissolved the Senator David Mark-led leadership of the party and invalidate its presidential candidacy as “a dangerous escalation in what appears to be a systematic campaign to eliminate credible political opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections.” In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman, on behalf of the coalition parties, the group warned that what is happening to the ADC today can happen to every opposition party tomorrow. The Coalition for Democracy emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August 2026. Its members are the ADC, Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), National Rescue Movement (NRM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Youth Progressives Party (YPP). The platform describes itself as committed to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism and ensuring free, fair, credible and competitive elections. The Coalition recalled that it had only a day earlier raised the alarm over Nigeria’s shrinking democratic space, citing attacks on opposition supporters, obstruction of political activities and “the increasing weaponisation of state institutions against political competitors.” “When opposition parties are attacked on the streets, frustrated by state institutions, and threatened with elimination through judicial pronouncements, Nigerians must ask whether the ruling party still intends to face any meaningful opposition at the ballot box,” the statement said. The Coalition said it respects the independence of the judiciary and the right of aggrieved parties to seek legal redress, but insisted that “the courts must never become instruments through which political competition is extinguished. “Those who seek to destroy the opposition in order to guarantee their own victory must understand that they are not merely threatening political parties; they are threatening the very foundations of the Republic. A government that cannot tolerate opposition has lost the moral authority to call itself democratic. “When a government becomes more afraid of the opposition than it is accountable to the people, democracy itself is in danger”, the parties added. It warned that the narrowing of democratic space “carries grave consequences for national stability,” adding: “No democracy can remain peaceful when citizens are denied meaningful political alternatives. “The ballot must remain the battlefield of democracy. No political party should be allowed to achieve through institutional manipulation what it fears it cannot achieve through the votes of Nigerians,” it said. item.title: Igbokoda air crash: NAF recovers cockpit voice recorder
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has recorded further progress in the recovery and investigation of the ATR-42 aircraft accident in Igbokoda, Ondo State, with the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), confirmed intact by technical teams from the NAF and Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB). Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, Director of Public Relations and Information disclosed this in a statement on Friday. He said, “Part of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), commonly referred to as the black box, was also retrieved, while efforts to locate and recover its remaining portion continue. “Additional aircraft wreckage, engine components and human remains have also been recovered. “Operations are ongoing in the challenging swamp terrain, with teams working to retrieve outstanding components and facilitate the necessary technical examinations. “The investigation is being conducted with due diligence to ensure comprehensive, evidence-based findings. “The recovery process also involves careful attention to the proper handling of human remains, with the Directorate of Identification and Classification (DIC) undertaking the necessary procedures for proper identification. “The NAF has sustained engagements with the families of the victims, recognising their need for information and support. “Engagement with relevant authorities on environmental concerns raised by the host community also remains an important part of the broader response. “While appreciating the public’s concern and interest, the NAF appeals for continued patience and understanding as these critical processes require time, careful coordination and professional attention. “The ultimate objective is not only to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident but also to draw the necessary lessons to strengthen flight safety, enhance ongoing airpower operations and further safeguard the lives of personnel and citizens. “The NAF remains committed to providing verified updates as appropriate.” The post Igbokoda air crash: NAF recovers cockpit voice recorder appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Troops nab notorious terrorist in Kaduna
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma, have arrested a suspected terrorist during an intelligence-led operation in Kagarko town, Kagarko Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The troops have also intensified air and ground operations to neutralise terrorists and deny them freedom of action in Zamfara State. Spokesman, Captain Tamuno Sinivie while making this known on Friday said, “On 5 November 2026, troops of Sector 1, in conjunction with operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), apprehended a suspected terrorist identified as Auta Maikyala during an intelligence-led operation. “The suspect was arrested at a hospital in Kagarko, where he had reportedly gone to seek medical attention for a gunshot wound sustained during an encounter with a rival faction. “Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect is an alleged notorious criminal who has been involved in several attacks on communities, kidnapping and cattle rustling operations. “He is currently in custody for further investigation and prosecution. “Similarly, troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have intensified clearance operations aimed at neutralising terrorists and dismantling their hideouts in Zamfara State. “On 5 November 2026, troops conducted clearance operations at Aljummu Hausa, Aljummu Fulani and Tunga Magaji villages in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. “The ongoing operations have resulted in the clearance of several terrorist hideouts, further restricting the activities of criminal elements and enhancing the security of residents in the affected communities. “In a related development, on the same day, the Air Component of the Nigerian Air Force, conducted air interdiction operations against identified terrorist locations suspected to be associated with the wanted terrorist kingpin, Dogo Gide, in Babban Doka and Kuyumbana Forest, Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State. “The operation followed credible intelligence indicating that the terrorists were assembling in the area to plan and coordinate their criminal activities. “Troops are currently maintaining dominance over the general area. ‘Operation Fansan Yamma will sustain its operational tempo and aggressive posture to fulfil its mandate of protecting lives and property across the Joint Operations Area. “The general public is urged to continue supporting ongoing military operations by providing timely and credible information on suspected terrorists and their activities to assist security agencies in eliminating criminal threats from our communities.” The post Troops nab notorious terrorist in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‎2027 Poll: INEC uncovers plot to kidnap ad-hoc staff, warns officers against partisanship
item.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja ‎ The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has uncovered an alleged plot to threaten, intimidate and kidnap ad-hoc electoral personnel, including members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), ahead of the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed that intelligence-led operations had led to the arrest of suspected kingpins allegedly behind the plot, adding that the suspects had been charged to court through the Department of State Services (DSS). Amupitan warned that anyone who threatened or harmed electoral personnel would face the full weight of the law. He also cautioned electoral officers against partisanship and administrative negligence, insisting that personnel found wanting in the discharge of their duties would face appropriate sanctions. The INEC chairman spoke in Lokoja during the commission’s North Central zonal operational readiness assessment and interactive staff engagement, where he stressed that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend largely on the neutrality, professionalism and commitment of personnel at the grassroots. He said the commission was strengthening collaboration with security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) framework to identify and address potential threats before the polls. According to him, INEC is also deploying Election Risk Management tools to identify vulnerable areas across the North Central zone and share the findings with security agencies for early intervention. Amupitan said the commission was intensifying preparations nationwide to ensure that the 2027 general election was better managed than previous electoral exercises, stressing that credible polls could not be achieved through last-minute preparations. He said INEC must sustain its operational readiness through adequate logistics, technological investment, staff welfare and improved administrative processes long before election day. The chairman said the commission was preparing for an election involving more than 103 million registered voters and 176,846 polling units across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. He disclosed that the North Central zone, comprising six states and the FCT, had a combined 15.44 million registered voters, with Kogi State accounting for 1,932,654. Describing the zone as strategically important to the electoral process, Amupitan said Kogi’s geographical position and borders with several states made its logistics, security and operational readiness critical to election administration. He charged electoral officers to ensure that no eligible voter was disenfranchised through administrative lapses or logistics failures, urging them to uphold neutrality, professionalism and accountability. item.title: Uzbekistan places temporary visa ban on Nigerians
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced temporary restrictions on visa issuance and entry for Nigerian citizens. A notice on the website of the Green Energy Technologies Central Asia (GETCA) exhibition states that restrictions have been introduced on the issuance of visas and entry into Uzbekistan for Nigerian nationals. The notice reads: “Temporary restrictions have currently been introduced on the issuance of visas and entry into the Republic of Uzbekistan for citizens of your country.” It also advises Nigerians seeking entry under exceptional circumstances to contact the consular section of the Embassy of Uzbekistan for further information. Nigeria is also not the only country listed under the temporary restrictions on the exhibition website. Other countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, Iraq and Bangladesh, also have similar notices. As of Friday, no formal public statement explaining the restrictions had been identified on the website of Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The ministry’s general visa information page provides details of the country’s visa arrangements for foreign nationals but does not specifically explain the reported restrictions affecting Nigerians. The development could affect Nigerians planning to visit the Central Asian country for tourism, business, education and other purposes. Affected travellers have been advised to contact the Uzbek embassy’s consular section to establish whether they qualify for exceptional entry arrangements. item.title: NYSC members’ kidnap: Court fixes Dec 16 for judgment
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara, Owerri An Imo State High Court, presided over by Justice Emeka Orafu, will deliver judgement in the suit, HOU/22C/2026, preferred against Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu, and Mohamed Ali, for their alleged involvement in the kidnap of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members, who were traveling to their orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom States. Justice Orafu disclosed this Friday, November 6, 2026, when the two defense lawyers announced closure of their case after the third witness, Mohammed Ali, DW3, finished testifying. The judge commended counsel on both sides for “responding very well” as the matter progressed. He gave the defense seven days, with effect from Saturday, November 7, 2026, to file their briefs, and the prosecution five days, with effect from Saturday, November 14, 2026, to file his response. Before adjourning the matter to November 24, 2026, for the adoption of their addresses, Justice Orafu fixed December 16, 2026, for the delivery of judgement. Testifying earlier, the DW3, who was led in evidence by his counsel, Mr. Paschal Oforma, told the court that he hails from Kogi State and tends his cow in Kara, Aba. He also told the court that he knows nothing about the kidnap but was arrested while sitting at Kara by the DSS, brought to Owerri, and detained. Asked by his counsel if he had any other thing to tell the court, DW3 denied knowing the other defendants. Cross-examined by the Director of Public Prosecution, DPP, Mr. Martins Udolwu, the DW3 said he has lived in Aba for about two years, accepted being a herdsman, but does not enter any forest. He told the court that he has two boys that take the cows out in the morning and bring them back in the evening. Answering another question, DW3 confirmed that he knows the DW1, adding that he sees him in the mosque but doesn’t know the DW2. The court erupted in laughter when DW3 quickly withdrew his submission that he was beaten before the audio-visual recording was done and said the DSS tried to beat him, but they didn’t, before the audio-visual confessional recording. Responding to the question put to him by counsel to DW1 and DW2, he said that he wrote one statement, filled one form in the presence of his counsel. item.title: Beyond the Final Score: The Data Signals That Move Sports Betting Markets
item.description: Everyone is always trying to beat sports betting markets but it isn’t always easy. That’s because behind every shift in a spread, moneyline or player prop is a constant stream of information being assessed by bookmakers, traders and bettors. With the growing influence of real-time data available in 2026, this has made understanding those signals increasingly important for anyone following sports markets. Let’s go through a few key ones to get you up to speed. The players Player availability remains one of the most powerful market-moving factors. A late injury , unexpected scratch or change to a starting line-up at the last minute can dramatically alter odds before a game begins. The effect is particularly noticeable in sports where one player has a large influence on team performance. Even before official confirmation, credible reports circulating on social media or reports from a trusted source about a player’s status can fluctuate odds as markets anticipate the potential impact. If you’re looking to bet on sports at Spinoli it’s important to note that recent performance data also matters although context is definitely crucial. A team’s last five games may tell part of the story, but bettors and analysts increasingly look deeper. Shot quality, possession, efficiency, yards per play, expected goals and other underlying metrics can reveal whether recent results are sustainable long term or whether they have been fortunate over a short period. So, while the final score records what happened, advanced data can provide clues about why it turned out a particular way. Another important signal is market movement itself. When prices shift across multiple sportsbooks or exchanges, that movement can indicate that new information has entered the market before it has reached the public domain. A recent example from UFC betting showed just how dramatic those movements can become, with the odds for Sean Brady vs. Joaquin Buckley shifting sharply before the fight. Comparing prices across platforms can therefore provide a useful snapshot of how market expectations are changing – and help to explain why. Consider the conditions Weather and venue conditions can also influence certain markets. Wind, rain, temperature and playing-surface conditions may be particularly relevant when it comes to betting on football, baseball, golf alongside other outdoor sports. Rather than ignoring the weather forecast, sophisticated models can incorporate it into projections for scoring, player performance and even the tempo of the match. The growing role of live data has made these signals even more dynamic. During a game, markets can react to possession changes, shots, fouls, player substitutions, pitch position and other events within seconds. Prediction markets have added another dimension to this process with contract prices providing a continuously updated indication of how traders assess an outcome. item.title: US Midterm: People Voted Based On Issues On Kitchen Tables, Not Party Slogans — Rep-Elect Adeyina
item.description: Member-elect of the Georgia House of Representatives (District 110) in the United States, Segun Adeyina, has said that Americans voted in the 2026 midterm elections based on the issues affecting their daily lives rather than political party slogans. “Well, of course it boils down to what’s going on in people’s kitchen tables. People did not vote based on political slogans. People voted on issues happening on their kitchen tables,” Adeyina said during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Friday. “Can they pay their rent, their mortgage? Can they afford groceries? Can they access healthcare? These are all important items that the everyday person has been faced with over the last couple of years.” ﻿ On how President Donald Trump’s performance impacted the big win for the Democrats, he said the war in Iran came at a cost to American families. “And Affordability was really one of the key issues that the president couldn’t truly address; and going to Iran, for us, drove up our costs, drove up the challenge that we have with affordability. “And it boiled down to what are the things that people discuss at their kitchen tables. And you see the outcome. The outcome was, you know, some people call it a blue wave. I call it a blue tsunami. “People showed up and turned out to vote on issues that concerned them on their kitchen tables.” The representative said that his re-election showed the confidence that voters in House District 110 have in his leadership. “I am a proud Nigerian-American, and this victory is very important. I was elected, as you know, in 2022, and that was a way to introduce myself to my community,” the representative said. “But being re-elected for the second time and serving a third term tells you the confidence that the people of House District 110, which consists of Grayson, Snowville, Lawrenceville, and Loganville, have in the opportunity that I have presented them, and coming back for a third term, it shows that they have confidence in the leadership and the service that I have provided.” Adeyia was among Nigerian-Americans who secured electoral victories in the November 3 midterm elections. Other successful candidates are Will Jawando, Junior Ezeonu, Oye Owolewa, Solomon Adesanya, Carol Kazeem, and Gab Okoye, who won seats in local government and state legislatures across Maryland, Texas, Washington, DC, Georgia, and Pennsylvania. item.title: FG seeks seven-year ban on establishing new federal universities, polytechnics
item.description: …Alausa tells Senate to stop approving establishment bills, cites NN1.3trn ASUU revitalisation debt, infrastructure deficits By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has moved to halt the establishment of new federal universities, polytechnics and colleges of education for seven years, warning that Nigeria risks expanding its tertiary education system at the expense of academic quality and the survival of existing institutions. The government said it could no longer afford to spread scarce resources across an increasing number of institutions while existing federal tertiary institutions grapple with severe funding shortages, decaying infrastructure, inadequate manpower and overcrowded classrooms. Consequently, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has appealed to the Senate and other members of the National Assembly to stop considering and passing bills seeking to establish additional federal tertiary institutions during the seven-year moratorium. The appeal was contained in a November 2, 2026, memo addressed to Senate President Godswill Akpabio and copied to Senate Majority Leader Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele. In the memo, marked FME/DUE/NASS/153/Vol.1/147 and sighted in Abuja on Friday, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Executive Council had approved the seven-year moratorium at its August 13, 2025, meeting as part of efforts to address the proliferation of public tertiary institutions, duplication of academic programmes and under-utilisation of existing facilities. The minister’s intervention comes amid persistent concerns over the government’s ability to adequately finance existing universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, with billions of naira in outstanding revitalisation commitments yet to be met. Making a case for the policy, Alausa argued that Nigeria’s immediate challenge was no longer the multiplication of tertiary institutions but the strengthening of those already established to deliver quality education. He warned that continuing to establish new institutions without guaranteed funding would deepen the crisis in the sector, potentially leaving more institutions struggling to provide basic academic facilities and services. “The Federal Government’s position is that the immediate challenge confronting the tertiary education sector is not merely the expansion of access but the urgent need to strengthen existing institutions,” he stated. According to him, the moratorium would allow the government to consolidate previous investments, address existing deficiencies and improve the carrying capacity of operational institutions before considering further expansion. Alausa expressed concern that despite the government’s policy direction, bills seeking the establishment of additional federal tertiary institutions continued to receive legislative attention. item.title: FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Saturday, November 7, as they seek to make history by winning their first title. The final, which will be the 52nd and last match of the tournament, will kick off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat. The encounter will be the first meeting between Nigeria and Japan at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first time the two countries face each other in a global final. Where to watch Nigeria vs Japan Football fans can watch the final live and for free through FIFA+, with streaming available via DAZN. How Nigeria reached the final Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. How Japan reached the final Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal. Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory. They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea. Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Players to watch For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats. Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition. Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions. What the coaches and captains said Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy. “We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.” Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter. “We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. Now we have just one more match to win, and we’re determined to make history.” Nigeria

item.title: INEC: 116,745 newly registered voters yet to collect PVCs in Lagos
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Lagos State says 116,745 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) of newly registered voters are yet to be collected. The Administrative Secretary of INEC in Lagos, Mrs Adenike Tadese, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Friday. Tadese said that the commission had received 177,295 PVCs belonging to eligible residents registered during Phase One of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise in 2025. She said the commission’s weekly update as of Monday showed that 60,550 PVCs had been collected by their owners, leaving 116,745 cards awaiting collection. According to her, the uncollected cards represent a significant number of eligible voters who should collect their PVCs to exercise their franchise in the 2027 general elections. She said the cards were available for collection at the various local government offices of the commission across the state. “The cards are available for collection by their owners, not by proxy, at the various local government offices of the commission in Lagos,” she said. Tadese urged stakeholders to mobilise both old registrants who have not collected their cards and those who participated in the 2025 CVR exercise to collect their PVCs. She said the cards were still lying at INEC offices and appealed to their owners to collect them before the collection window closed ahead of the forthcoming elections. The INEC official also disclosed that PVCs belonging to eligible residents who registered during the 2026 CVR exercise before its closure would soon be ready for collection. Tadese, however, urged eligible registered voters to maintain orderliness during the collection of their PVCs. She reaffirmed the commission’s readiness to conduct free, fair and credible elections that would be acceptable to all stakeholders in the state. The administrative secretary also called for peaceful and orderly campaigns, urging all stakeholders to abide by the rules guiding the electoral process. She appealed to political actors and other stakeholders to play by the rules to ensure a peaceful electoral environment ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Family Sues Google Over Teenager’s Suicide-Related AI Chats On School Computer
item.description: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant’s low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world. The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was not able to access Google’s Gemini app, nor OpenAI’s ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google’s search engine, which contains AI-powered tools. Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students. Google on March 21, 2023 invited people in the United States and Britain to test its AI chatbot, known as Bard, as it scrambles to catch up with Microsoft-backed ChatGPT. (Photo by Pau BARRENA / AFP) “Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they’re interacting with AI,” Andrew Liddell, one of the family’s attorneys, told AFP on Thursday. The complaint alleges that Emma had been a “happy 13-year-old girl” in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts. Despite “no history” of mental illness, within months of using Google’s AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a “quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis” according to the complaint. On March 17, the school’s monitoring software flagged a document titled “Funeral,” and the school notified her parents. Her mother then saw Emma writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter’s account, and her father intervened. “We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously,” Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP. Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them. But Emma “was able to keep going back over and over and over again,” Liddle said. “Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient.” Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US. OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including from the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who committed suicide allegedly using methods advised by ChatGPT. Google and the startup Character.AI agreed in January to settle several lawsuits filed by families of teenagers out of court. On Wednesday, Google, TikTok and Meta each separately sued California to block a law that prohibits social media companies from providing addictive features to users under 16. Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law in September, and it goes into effect on January 1, 2027.
